title: AdapterFusion over Mirror-compressed adapters
hypothesis: Per-task Givens coordinates over shared low-rank factors preserve AdapterFusion composition quality while reducing serialized bytes versus independent adapters and generic shared-basis coefficients.
physical_object: shared input/output factors A (rank6 x 32) and B (32 x rank6), with four logical source adapters
mirror_coordinate: fifteen per-task Givens angles parameterizing an orthogonal 6x6 rank-space transform C_t in B C_t A
logical_multiplicity: four source adapters consumed by a contextual AdapterFusion gate
controls: independent rank-6 source adapters + common learned fusion gate
shared A/B basis with generic per-task 6x6 coefficient matrices + same fusion gate
Mirror shared A/B plus six Givens angles per adapter + same gate
teacher: four source maps B C_t A with common B/A and C_t generated by fifteen fixed Givens rotations; composition target is input-softmax mixture of all four source outputs

development.selection_metric: fusion held-out MSE normalized by target variance

fresh.run_only_if: both dev worlds pass all quality and actual-byte gates

storage.format: torch.save all source factors/codes, fusion gate, and metadata
paid_objects: all adapter factors or shared basis
per-task full coefficient matrices or Mirror angles

compute.proxy: rank6 projection plus task-specific rank transform and fusion, per input across four source adapters; report angle transform overhead

success_gate: Fresh fusion NRMSE <=1.10x independent full adapter bank in both worlds; Mirror bytes <=0.75x full bank and <=0.90x generic shared-basis control.
failure_gate: Any development quality or actual-byte gate fails; fresh remains sealed.
boundaries: Teacher is intentionally aligned to an orthogonal Givens orbit.
This experiment does not establish arbitrary adapter/task compression or natural-task transfer.
Fusion composition evaluates all four source adapter outputs in every variant.
